what_this_is: Figures that were published and turned out to be wrong. Each one is recorded here so it cannot come back. scripts/check-retired-figures.py fails the build if a retired value reappears anywhere near its own subject.
why: Every wrong figure on this hub so far was found by a person reading a page, not by a check. The register catches a hero figure no script owns, and check-consistency catches MASTER_DATA drifting from a feed, but nothing stopped a figure that had already been corrected once from being re-typed somewhere else. Three of the figures below were corrected on 2026-09-30 and were still live on another page three weeks later.
how_to_add: When you correct a published figure, add an entry here in the same commit. 'wrong' lists every written form of the bad value. 'context' is a regex that must appear within context_window characters for a hit to count, so an unrelated use of the same digits does not fail the build. Set context_window wide enough to clear any correction note sitting between the subject and the figure -- 900 is the working default; 200 missed a live error on its first run.

skip_after_heading.note: The update log records what was corrected, so it necessarily names the old value. It is a history, not a claim.

retired.subject: HomeBASE (7004-0108) actual spending, FY2026
retired.right: $57.29M ($57,286,763) — CTHRU kv7m-35wn, account 70040108, fiscal_year 2026, total_expenses
retired.why: Published as a CTHRU actual. CTHRU's actual for that account and year is $57,286,763. The $91,386,678 figure is from a different source — the FY27 budget documents' FY2026 projected column — and was carried into the CTHRU series as though it were an actual.
retired.allow_note: method.html is generated from MASTER_DATA.md and renders its update log. Its register rows are checked upstream by update-immigrant-spending.py, which writes them. MASTER_DATA.md keeps the budget-document projection as its own clearly labelled row, because the distinction between a projection and an actual is the thing that went wrong and the register is where it has to be recorded. update-immigrant-spending.py names the figure in the comment explaining why it writes this series. scripts/check-cross-page.py names the figure in the docstring explaining what the check exists to catch.

retired.subject: transfers into HomeBASE (7004-0108), FY2026
retired.right: $2,575 — CTHRU kv7m-35wn transfer_in for account 70040108, fiscal_year 2026
retired.why: This was not read from CTHRU. $91,386,678 minus the $57,322,001 appropriation is $34,064,677 — the figure was derived from the gap between two incompatible sources and then described as a transfer, which made the contradiction look explained. CTHRU's transfer_in field for that account and year is $2,575.
retired.allow_note: Same rows: the register states the arithmetic that produced the false transfer, so a reader can see it was derived rather than read. scripts/check-cross-page.py names the figure in the docstring explaining what the check exists to catch.

retired.subject: MIRA Coalition lobbying, 2022-2025
retired.right: $451,299 total 2020-2026 (salaries, firm payments and expenses); salaries alone 2022-2025 are $86,971.60
retired.why: Counted salaries only, and excluded payments to Charles Group Consulting and reported expenses, which understated the money by about 5x. Read from the Secretary of the Commonwealth's Lobbyist Public Search on 2026-10-21. The abbreviated form ($87.5K) sat in a callout beside the corrected paragraph and was missed on the first pass: the correction note itself is ~700 characters, so the subject word was outside a 300-character window. Hence 900. It also survived in DECOMPOSED form until 2026-10-21: the dashboard listed its four components ($61,132 + $20,000 + $4,626 + $1,790) as a 'Registered Lobbyists' table, and no cell on the page held $87,548 so this check could not see it. A retired figure split across four cells is still the retired figure. Replaced by the registry's own per-year totals, which reconcile to the $451,299 headline.
retired.allow_note: scripts/stamp-mira-lobbying.py names the figure in the docstring explaining what it replaced and why.
